_about: Tables for world/POPULATION.md. The aggregate settlement model: a pool of unnamed people a town draws from. It never writes a named character's fate (town/UPGRADES.md, balance/ALIGNMENT.md and BALANCE.md own fates). Historical rates from Wrigley and Schofield (England) and Burnard (Jamaica). mark: rex | proposed | open. Tables moved whole to data/library/population.json (no game columns): cohorts, tick.

rates.title: Historical vital rates (per 1,000 per year)
rates.source: England 1690s to 1720s: births about 28 to 33, deaths about 26 to 28, life expectancy at birth 35 to 38, a crisis year (1726) with deaths near 37 (Wrigley and Schofield via the Toronto tables; POP-WS). Jamaica: white deaths far above births; 50,000 Europeans arrived 1700 to 1750 and the white population grew by about 5,000; median settler marriage about six years (Burnard; POP-BURN). Port Royal 1692: about 6,500 people, about 2,000 killed in the earthquake and 3,000 more of injury and disease after (POP-PR). Enslaved populations in the sugar islands also fell without imports (Burnard, general).
